Vikramaditya I.fact: The defeated Chalukyan army was led by Vikramaditya's son and grandson Vinayaditya and Vijayaditya. The combined forces of these four powers entered the Chalukyan territory and probably sacked and captured Vatapi 'the city of Ranarasika ’ on this occasion.

Vikramaditya I.fact: Kumud Chitalia observes that Chalukya inscriptions are silent regarding Siruthondar's alleged expedition and instead credit Vinayāditya with restoring order during Vikramāditya I's southern campaign. K. K. Dasgupta likewise states that while Pallava records refer to pressure on Ranarasika's city, Chalukya records credit Vinayāditya and Vijayāditya with defeating the invading forces, adding that whether Badami itself was actually threatened cannot be set up with certainty.

Vikramaditya I.subject: Indian Languages

Vikramaditya I.fact: The Chalukyan empire however had put the worst behind under Vikramaditya I and recovered most of its territories it controlled under Pulakeshin II. Some historians compare him to his illustrious father Pulakeshin II.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: The _____ was 1914–1921 Franco-Berber war in Morocco.
Zaian War.fact: After seven years of fighting the Zaian War was ended, though Lyautey continued his expansion in the area, promising to have all of "useful Morocco" under French control by 1923.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: The Zaian (or Zayan) War was fought between France and the Zaian Confederation of Berber tribes in Morocco between _____ and 1921 during the French conquest of Morocco
Zaian War.fact: The Zaian (or Zayan) War was fought between France and the Zaian Confederation of Berber tribes in Morocco between 1914 and 1921 during the French conquest of Morocco.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Morocco had become a French protectorate in _____, and Resident-General Louis-Hubert Lyautey sought to extend French influence eastwards through the Middle Atlas mountains towards French Algeria
Zaian War.fact: Morocco had become a French protectorate in 1912, and Resident-General Louis-Hubert Lyautey sought to extend French influence eastwards through the Middle Atlas mountains towards French Algeria.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: This was opposed by the _____, led by Mouha ou Hammou Zayani
Zaian War.fact: This was opposed by the Zaians, led by Mouha ou Hammou Zayani. Despite the loss of their base at Khénifra, the Zaians inflicted heavy losses on the French, who responded by establishing groupes mobiles, combined arms formations that mixed regular and irregular infantry, cavalry and artillery into a single force.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: The war began well for the _____, who quickly took the key towns of Taza and Khénifra
Zaian War.fact: The Zaian (or Zayan) War was fought between France and the Zaian Confederation of Berber tribes in Morocco between 1914 and 1921 during the French conquest of Morocco. Morocco had become a French protectorate in 1912, and Resident-General Louis-Hubert Lyautey sought to extend French influence eastwards through the Middle Atlas mountains towards French Algeria.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: The outbreak of the _____ proved significant, with the withdrawal of troops for service in France compounded by the loss of more than 600 French killed at the Battle of El Herri
Zaian War.fact: The outbreak of the First World War proved significant, with the withdrawal of troops for service in France compounded by the loss of more than 600 French killed at the Battle of El Herri.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: After the signing of the Armistice with Germany in November _____, significant forces of tribesmen remained opposed to French rule
Zaian War.fact: After the signing of the Armistice with Germany in November 1918, significant forces of tribesmen remained opposed to French rule.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: The French resumed their offensive in the Khénifra area in _____, establishing a series of blockhouses to limit the Zaians' freedom of movement
Zaian War.fact: The French resumed their offensive in the Khénifra area in 1920, establishing a series of blockhouses to limit the Zaians' freedom of movement.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: They opened negotiations with _____'s sons, persuading three of them, along with many of their followers, to submit to French rule
Zaian War.fact: They opened negotiations with Hammou's sons, persuading three of them, along with many of their followers, to submit to French rule. A split in the Zaian Confederation between those who supported submission and those still opposed led to infighting and the death of Hammou in Spring 1921.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: A split in the Zaian Confederation between those who supported submission and those still opposed led to infighting and the death of Hammou in Spring _____
Zaian War.fact: A split in the Zaian Confederation between those who supported submission and those still opposed led to infighting and the death of Hammou in Spring 1921.

Zaian War.question: The French responded with a strong, three-pronged attack into the _____ that pacified the area
Zaian War.fact: The French responded with a strong, three-pronged attack into the Middle Atlas that pacified the area.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Some tribesmen, led by Moha ou Said, fled to the _____ and continued a guerrilla war against the French well into the 1930s
Zaian War.fact: Some tribesmen, led by Moha ou Said, fled to the High Atlas and continued a guerrilla war against the French well into the 1930s.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.fact: Al-Hiba escaped to the Atlas mountains with a small number of his followers and opposed French rule until his death in 1919.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: A popular idea among the public in France was to possess an unbroken stretch of territory from Tunis to the _____, including expansion into the "Taza corridor" in the Moroccan interior
Zaian War.fact: A popular idea among the public in France was to possess an unbroken stretch of territory from Tunis to the Atlantic Ocean, including expansion into the "Taza corridor" in the Moroccan interior.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Lyautey was in favour of this and advocated French occupation of the _____ mountains near Taza, through peaceful means where possible
Zaian War.fact: Lyautey was in favour of this and advocated French occupation of the Middle Atlas mountains near Taza, through peaceful means where possible. This French expansion into the Middle Atlas was strongly opposed by the "powerful Berber trinity" of Mouha ou Hammou Zayani, leader of the Zaian Confederation; Moha ou Said, leader of the Aït Ouirra; and Ali Amhaouch, a religious leader of the Darqawa variant of Islam prevalent in the region.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.fact: Hammou commanded between 4,000 and 4,200 tents of people and had led the Zaians since 1877, opposing the French since the start of their involvement in Morocco.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.fact: Hammou commanded between 4,000 and 4,200 tents of people and had led the Zaians since 1877, opposing the French since the start of their involvement in Morocco. Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.fact: The French had attempted to persuade the Zaians to submit since 1913 with little success; most tribes in the confederation remained opposed to French rule.

Zaian War.fact: He had been advised by his political officer, Maurice Le Glay that doing so would "finish him off definitively" and cut the Zaians off from support of other tribes.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.fact: Henrys captured Taza within a few days using units drawn from garrisons in Fez, Meknes, Rabat and Marrakesh and then turned his attention to Khénifra.

Henrys took overall command, directing the forces from an armoured car within the Claudel column.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Despite these measures, _____'s column came under attack before it even left Meknes, although it was the largest and intended as a diversion
Zaian War.fact: Henrys took overall command, directing the forces from an armoured car within the Claudel column. Despite these measures, Claudel's column came under attack before it even left Meknes, although it was the largest and intended as a diversion.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Further attacks on the nights of 14 and 15 _____ were repulsed by artillery and machine gun fire, directed by searchlights
Zaian War.fact: The rest of the column joined them on 12 June, fighting off Zaian attacks on the way and meeting up with the other two columns, finding the town emptied of people and raising the French flag. Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: South of el Bordj the _____ came under heavy fire from tribesmen with modern rifles and resorted to bayonet charges to clear the way
Zaian War.fact: In response all French-controlled markets were closed to the Zaians and their trade convoys were intercepted. South of el Bordj the French came under heavy fire from tribesmen with modern rifles and resorted to bayonet charges to clear the way.

Zaian War.question: Henrys became aware of a Zaian presence at el _____ and sent a column to attack them on 31 June
Zaian War.fact: Henrys became aware of a Zaian presence at el Bordj and sent a column to attack them on 31 June. South of el Bordj the French came under heavy fire from tribesmen with modern rifles and resorted to bayonet charges to clear the way.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.fact: Henrys became aware of a Zaian presence at el Bordj and sent a column to attack them on 31 June. The encounter was Henrys' first major engagement with the Zaians and his losses were high, 1 officer and 16 men killed and a further 2 officers and 75 men wounded.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Zaian losses were much higher: the _____ counted at least 140 dead remaining on the battlefield, and considered the battle a victory
Zaian War.fact: South of el Bordj the French came under heavy fire from tribesmen with modern rifles and resorted to bayonet charges to clear the way. Zaian losses were much higher: the French counted at least 140 dead remaining on the battlefield, and considered the battle a victory.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.fact: His plan depended on holding a "living barricade" of French outposts running from Taza in the north through Khenifra, Kasbah Tadla and Marrakesh to Agadir on the Atlantic coast.
